rapport_notes: Calvin is warm, attentive, and patient; uses the customer's name naturally and responds to her concerns with genuine empathy about her prior bad experience.
process_discipline_notes: Wrapped/damage coverage mentioned twice (Stage 1 as direct concern response + Stage 2 in pricing pitch); no silence held after 'does that all kind of make sense' — rep moves immediately into pricing detail.

evidence_quotes.agenda: NOT ASKED — rep never asks 'other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move, and what do you want answers to on this call?' Instead jumps directly to logistics after initial greeting.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer spontaneously raises damage concern ('they broke my dining room chair...scratched up') but rep does not probe deeper into other concerns; rep pivots to offering solution (wrapping policy) without follow-up dig. No other concerns raised during discovery.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Stage 1 direct answer: 'Yeah, no, we wrap everything. So, yeah, that's wrap pads and wrap are included in our rate...anything that couldn't get scratched we do wrap that is company policy.' Also mentioned in Stage 2 pricing section: 'everything is fully insured...we have our no worries damage coverage that's included in the hourly rate it allocates up to $2,000 per move.'
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Stage 2 delivery: 'and then all of our movers too. They are background check. They are trained in-house...They're on our website. Everyone's got their picture and bio up there. We send a little meet your movers email a couple of days before the move to let you know who there'll be.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Stage 2 delivery: 'we also do have an on time guarantee if we're ever late to a window of arrival that we give you, we do discount your money back.'
evidence_quotes.communication: Stage 2 delivery: 'we also check-in the day before and a couple of days in advance with an email and a text' and 'They call that morning when they're on the way.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full range with personalization: 'the first story typically will be in the range with two guys of about three to five hours. So, in the range of about $576 to about $960 is the standard kind of estimated cost that we see for a move like this.' [personalized to two-bedroom, single-story, 20-30 boxes]
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_commit: 'we do things the right way and if we make mistakes we make them that's kind of why we have a good reputation isn't just always being perfect but if anything happens, you know, you're fully covered by us'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_window: 'you do just pay for the time that's actually used that day' and later 'when they get there, they'll run through the contract with you...the time is all tracked on the iPad and then at the end they'll stop the clock'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_beats_it: 'and then we bill in fifteen minute increments until the move is completed so you do just pay for the time that's actually used that day.'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_self_prep: 'Anything that can get jostled and lost as best removed from the drawers. But the soft goods it's usually okay to keep it in.'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_fair_silence: Rep says 'So, did you want to just get on the calendar for that date?' — customer says 'Yeah' but rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' and does not hold silence; instead transitions immediately into payment logistics discussion.
evidence_quotes.close: No rate-lock line mentioned. No explicit ask like 'would you like our help with your move?' — the close is transactional: 'So, did you want to just get on the calendar for that date?' Customer agrees, but there is no intentional sales close, only scheduling confirmation.

top_strength: Exceptional handling of the customer's prior damage trauma—Calvin pivoted smoothly from logistics into a direct, empathetic answer about Einstein's wrapping policy and damage coverage, addressing her stated concern before she had to ask twice, which rebuilt her trust.
coaching_note: Critical gap: never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' — you caught the damage concern only because she volunteered it; the rubric asks you to surface hidden concerns proactively, and without that line, you miss the chance to uncover and dig two layers deep into what matters most to Linda.
